title: normalize tool signatures and make streaming fragments tolerant to interleaved tool output
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a canonical tool/function signature normalizer for the OpenAI-compatibility layer and adds fragment-tolerance logic to the streaming framer so interleaved tool output (partial fragments, out-of-order frames, and repeated tool_choice hints) do not corrupt the upstream message envelope.

Motivation: Customers saw flaky behavior when tool_call payloads were split across streaming fragments or when LLMs emitted tool_choice hints multiple times during a response. In practice this manifested as duplicate invocations, truncated schemas, and frequent retries that degraded latency and user experience.

Goals:
1) Normalize incoming tool/function schemas to a predictable internal representation (canonical argument names, explicit optional/required markers, and stable ordering for equality checks).
2) Make the streaming framer idempotent when reassembling tool messages across fragments and robust to duplicated tool_choice tokens.
3) Emit deterministic telemetry and a small migration guide for downstream consumers.

Design:
- Signature normalizer (pkg/compat/openai/signature_normalizer.go) parses OpenAI-style function/tool schema objects and produces a compact canonical form: name, ordered args (name:type:required), and a checksum label used for fast equality checks. The normalizer tolerates synonyms (e.g., "params", "arguments"), coerces primitive JSON Schema variants, and drops non-serializable examples.
- Framer changes (pkg/serving/stream/framer.go): introduce a fragment buffer keyed by request-id + tool-call-id checksum; fragments are validated against the canonical signature before commit. Duplicate tool_choice hints are treated as idempotent votes — the first full message wins, later duplicates are logged but ignored.
- Message envelope tagging: add a light-weight tag on tool output frames (X-Tool-Canon: <checksum>) so downstream routers can match partials to canonical signatures without reparsing full schemas.
- Backwards compatibility: for any input that does not match canonicalization rules, the system falls back to the previous loose-envelope behavior and emits a compatibility metric (compat.signature_fallback).

Migration notes: No client changes required; however customers relying on exact byte-level tool payloads should pin to older SDK versions until they adopt checksum-based matching. The change is gated by a feature flag (compat_tool_normalizer=true) and will be rolled out in canary first.

Testing and observability:
- Unit tests: signature normalizer has exhaustive cases for nullable/optional fields and synonym maps.
- Integration tests: tests/integration/toolcall_replay_test.go simulates out-of-order fragments, duplicate tool_choice emissions, and interleaved non-tool text; all replay cases assert a single invocation and conserved schema.
- Telemetry: new counters (compat.signature_normalized, compat.signature_fallback) and a histogram for fragment_reassembly_latency.

Security: sanitization removes example/snippet fields from canonical payloads before any logs.

Checklist:
- [x] Parser implemented and tested
- [x] Framer accepts partial interleaved fragments
- [x] Telemetry added
- [x] Feature flag implemented
- [x] Docs and migration notes added
- [x] End-to-end test with live streaming harness

Commits summary:
- feat(compat): add signature normalizer and checksum generator
- feat(stream): fragment buffer keyed by request+checksum
- fix(stream): idempotent tool_choice handling on duplicate hints
- perf: avoid reparsing by caching canonical forms for 30s
- docs: note migration and feature-flag behavior

CI notes: initial CI run failed on a flaky integration asserting order; I reworked the test harness to use deterministic clock injection and re-ran. Final CI is green.

Merge strategy: squash and merge after approvals.
